title: Project One: Campus Event Finder
blurb: A full-stack app that actually pulls campus events into one place so people stop missing them.
listBlurb: Helps students find on-campus events filtered by interest, building, and date.
timeframe: Built this on my own over about 6 weeks, Spring 2026. In my project folder I just called it Nightowl.
alt: Screenshot of the Campus Event Finder app showing a filterable list of events
problem: Students at my school missed events they would have liked to attend simply because listings were scattered across five different club websites and a PDF calendar that was rarely updated.
approach: I built a single searchable events page that pulls listings into one place and lets students filter by interest tag, building, and date.
features: Filter events by tag, location, and date range
Simple submission form for club organizers
outcome: Around 40 students used the tool during its first week on campus, and two club officers asked to keep using it as their primary listing page.

title: Project Two: Habit Tracker
blurb: A small habit tracker I made because every other one felt overbuilt for what I actually needed.
listBlurb: A small habit-tracking tool with streaks and a weekly review.
timeframe: Built this on my own over about 3 weeks, Winter 2026.
alt: Screenshot of the Habit Tracker app showing a weekly grid of habits and streaks
problem: Most habit trackers I tried were either too simple (a bare checklist) or too complex (full analytics dashboards I never opened).
approach: I designed a minimal weekly grid: one row per habit, one column per day, and a streak counter that updates as you go.
features: Weekly grid view with one-tap check-off
Data stored entirely on-device, no account needed
outcome: I've used it daily for over two months, which is longer than any habit tracker I've tried before building my own.

title: Project Three: Recipe Box
blurb: A recipe manager so my family would stop texting each other blurry photos of index cards.
timeframe: Built this on my own over about 4 weeks, Fall 2025.
alt: Screenshot of the Recipe Box app showing a searchable grid of recipe cards
problem: My family's recipes were split between a shared folder of phone photos, a handful of bookmarked sites, and a few handwritten cards.
approach: I built a small app for entering recipes once, tagging them by cuisine and ingredient, and finding them again by searching any of those tags.
features: Tag-based search across ingredients and cuisine
Import form for adding new recipes quickly
outcome: The whole family now adds new recipes there instead of texting photos of index cards to each other.
